newsitem.title: FRANCE: French 1996 beet deliveries seen down on last year.
newsitem.headline: French 1996 beet deliveries seen down on last year.

text.p: French planters said on Wednesday they expected to deliver less sugar beet to refineries in the 1996/97 campaign than in the previous season.
They linked the expected decline to a drop in area sown and to a dry spring that limited beet development.

Data collected by the French sugar beet planters' association CGB up to October 15 showed some 35 percent of total beet area harvested and some 30 percent had been delivered to refineries, a CGB analyst told Reuters.
Sugar content at delivery was 18.7-18.8 percent, up from 17.5 percent last year.
But average beet yield was only 54 tonnes per hectare, down from a previous estimate of 56 tonnes and well below the 59.5 tonnes reached last year.
Assuming area fell to 422,000 hectares from 425,000 last year, total beet deliveries for 1996/97 may reach 22.7 million tonnes, down from 25.3 million last year.
Because there will be fewer beets to process this year, factories agreed to delay processing operations to October 1. Processing traditionally starts around September 28.
Dry soil conditions in late September initially slowed the pace of the harvest, but rain in the first half of October brought an improvement, planters said.
